reason: I'll start with filtering blood, since the picture shows small substances passing into the kidney while cells and large proteins stay in the vessels.
expectation: I expect a filtered fluid containing water, glucose, salts and waste, which may then go to the recovery tube.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the route to the bladder, but I want to follow filtration first.

effect: The filter also lets useful glucose, salts and water through, so the recovery tube is the next step.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The recovery tube is shown returning useful substances to the blood.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, leaving fluid containing wastes.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to finish following the filtered fluid first.

effect: The remaining fluid becomes urine after useful substances and much water return to the blood. Now I need to build its drainage route.
reaction: It makes sense that filtering and taking substances back are separate steps.
reason: The ureters lead from the kidneys toward the bladder, so I'll add them first.
expectation: I expect the two ureters to connect to the kidney outlets, leaving a place for the bladder.

alternatives.reason: I could add the bladder first, but following the route from the kidneys seems clearer.

effect: The ureters now lead from the kidneys toward the bladder position, leaving the bladder to add.
reaction: The muscular squeezes moving fluid along the tubes were a useful detail.
reason: Adding the bladder is the only available combination and completes the pictured drainage route.
expectation: I expect the bladder to connect to the ureters and receive urine.

effect: The bladder completes the route from both kidneys; urine collects there without changing into a different fluid.
reaction: The continuous fluid trail made the route easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering the blood and then recovering useful substances made the kidney's job clearer: the filter lets useful small substances through too.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the bladder was straightforward and was the only available combination, so it involved little decision-making, even though it completed the route.

surprise.text: The filter lets glucose and other useful substances through along with wastes, rather than picking out only waste.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the pictures explained both recovery and the drainage route.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter: following a familiar substance through filtering, recovery and drainage made the body connections interesting, even if the final fitting was predictable.
